requirement: Determine if there are known occurrences of any state or federally-listed species within the impact area of the project site.
source: Section 26-306 of the Regulations of Connecticut State Agencies

requirement: If the project site is in a documented area [for endangered species], consultation with DEEP’s NDDB staff will be required to agree upon impact-avoidance and protection measures.
scope: Project sites within documented endangered species areas
source: Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection (DEEP) Natural Diversity Data Base (NDDB)
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; endangered species protection

requirement: Protection measures will be included in a determination letter from DEEP; this letter must be included with filings for other state permit applications or general permit registrations.
scope: Project sites within documented endangered species areas
source: Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection (DEEP) Natural Diversity Data Base (NDDB)
related_domains: permitting; environmental impact assessment; endangered species protection

requirement: If a project involves disturbing an area greater than one acre during construction, [stormwater regulations apply].
source: Implied Connecticut Stormwater Regulations (exact source not specified in the provided text)
related_domains: stormwater management; construction; environmental impact assessment

requirement: Projects between one and five acres can comply with the Construction Stormwater General Permit by adhering to local land use requirements for erosion and sedimentation control; the 2002 Connecticut Guidelines for Soil Erosion and Sediment Control, as amended; and the Stormwater Quality Manual.
scope: Construction projects between one and five acres
source: DEEP General Permit for the Discharge of Stormwater and Dewatering Wastewaters from Construction Activities (Construction Stormwater General Permit)
related_domains: erosion control; sedimentation control; stormwater management

requirement: Eligible construction projects involving five or more acres of land disturbance and any project requiring Connecticut Siting Council approval must register for coverage under DEEP’s Construction Stormwater General Permit.
scope: Construction projects involving five or more acres of land disturbance and any project requiring Connecticut Siting Council approval

requirement: Wind turbine manufacturing activities may require coverage under DEEP’s General Permit for the Discharge of Stormwater Associated with Industrial Activity (Industrial Stormwater General Permit) if the activity generates a point source stormwater discharge.
source: DEEP’s General Permit for the Discharge of Stormwater Associated with Industrial Activity (Industrial Stormwater General Permit)

requirement: The Industrial Stormwater General Permit requires registration by the operator of the facility, development and implementation of a Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan, and stormwater discharge monitoring.
scope: Facilities operating under the Industrial Stormwater General Permit

requirement: Determinations regarding natural resources and other permit requirements (NDDB, forestry, wetlands, dam safety, flood management, brownfield remediation, landfills, etc.), are typically required for both stormwater general permits and inform the requirements for filing for a stormwater permit registration, and development of the requisite Stormwater Pollution Control Plan and/or Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan.
scope: Construction activities and industrial stormwater discharge
related_domains: stormwater management; environmental impact assessment; water pollution

requirement: At any time, the Commissioner can determine that a discharge associated with a construction activity or a stormwater discharge associated with an industrial activity requires an individual permit under the National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) program and Connecticut’s Water Pollution Control Act.
scope: Construction activities and industrial stormwater discharge
source: National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) program and Connecticut’s Water Pollution Control Act

requirement: If siting wind energy operations results in a direct discharge of fill material to wetlands or watercourses that meet the definition of waters of the United States, a permit from the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) is required.
scope: Discharge of fill material into US waters

requirement: Such activities require a Section 401 Water Quality Certification (WQC) from DEEP.
Coastal projects that impact tidal wetlands will require additional review and permitting in accordance with CGS Section 22a - 32 and RCSA Sections 22a - 30 - 1 to 22a - 30 - 10, inclusive.
source: CGS Section 22a - 32 and RCSA Sections 22a - 30 - 1 to 22a - 30 - 10
related_domains: environmental permitting; coastal zone management; wetland permitting

requirement: Wind energy projects on state property or that receive state funding, including grants or loans, that are located in a floodplain will require a Flood Management Certification from DEEP or an exemption from such certification requirements.
scope: Wind energy projects on state property or receiving state funding located in a floodplain
source: Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection (DEEP)

requirement: Residential and community structures in areas subject to coastal flooding be elevated two feet above the base flood elevation to account for projected sea level rise.
scope: Residential and community structures in 100-year coastal flood zone
source: Public Act 18-82, An Act Concerning Climate Change and Resiliency
related_domains: flood management; coastal resilience; building codes

requirement: activities within the coastal boundary, municipalities will be required to perform a coastal site plan review (CSPR) to ensure that the activity is consistent with the policies of the Connecticut Coastal Management Act
source: Connecticut Coastal Management Act [CGS Sections 22a-90 – 22a-110, inclusive]

requirement: compliance with the Remediation Standard Regulations, RCSA Sections 22a-133k-1 to 22a-133k-3, inclusive, is required
scope: Project sites subject to Property Transfer laws or other pollution release clean up requirements
source: Remediation Standard Regulations, RCSA Sections 22a-133k-1 to 22a-133k-3, inclusive

requirement: Marine Habitat Conservation Plan developed in conjunction with US Fish and Wildlife Service and DEEP
scope: Facilities with a generating capacity of more than 65 MW
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; marine habitat protection
